left.title: How to Secure Your Living Room Against Sentient Recliners
left.snippet: Following Sir Sits-a-Lot's unexpected rebellion, home-security groups recommend anchoring heavy chic chairs and avoiding retro googly eye modifications...
left.author: Mildred Jenkins
left.content:
With a rogue modern chair actively commanding armored armor plating across the Eastern Seaboard, homeowners are checking their own seating setups with newfound anxiety.

Security specialists suggest swapping out any wheeled legs with secure, heavy wooden block bases and refusing to let household recliners watch tactical military footage on television.

main.title: BREAKING NEWS: FURNITURE-GEDDON
main.imageAlt: Armored military tank causing urban disruption
main.snippet: WASHINGTON D.C. — Residents are advised to stay indoors and avoid looking directly into the 'shifty, plastic eyes of menace' as a mid-century modern accent chair has hijacked a military-grade tank, launching an 'unprecedented rampage' across the Eastern Seaboard...
main.author: Admiral Correspondent
main.content:
WASHINGTON D.C. — Residents are advised to stay indoors and avoid looking directly into the "shifty, plastic eyes of menace" as a mid-century modern accent chair has hijacked a military-grade tank, launching an "unprecedented rampage" across the Eastern Seaboard.

The chair, colloquially known on social media as "Sir Sits-a-Lot," was originally part of a chic Airbnb listing in Virginia before gaining sentience—or possibly just getting stuck in the mechanism of a runaway automated tank during a military parade.


"The Shaking is Real"

Witnesses describe a 57-ton M60 tank maneuvering through traffic with alarming agility, its turret spinning wildly while two large, 4-inch adhesive googly eyes stuck to the armored plating rattle aggressively, according to witness testimonies of past similar panics.

"It didn't stop at the red light," said Mildred Jenkins, who saw the chair-driven tank flatten a Starbucks. "It just stared at me with those unblinking, plastic pupils. The eyes… they shake, but they never look away. It's comforting and terrifying."


Nuke-Ready Mayhem

Military officials have confirmed that the tank is currently carrying four thermonuclear warheads, making this the most high-stakes, home-decor-related incident in history.

"We are dealing with a rogue recliner that has no respect for the chain of command," said Pentagon spokesperson Gen Barry Steel. "It's currently trying to log into the launch computer. We've changed the password to 'chair123,' but we fear it already knows that."


The Rampage Continues

The chair has so far ignored all pleas to return to its corner, instead taking scenic detours through local flowerbeds and attempting to run over a mail truck.

As of 3:00 PM EST, "Sir Sits-a-Lot" was spotted heading toward a furniture warehouse, presumably to "rescue its brethren."

Stay tuned for updates. In the meantime, if you see a tank with large, plastic eyes, please do not offer it a seat.

extraStory.title: Virginia Airbnb Host Issues Apology Over Escaped Recliner
extraStory.snippet: The host explains the mid-century modern accent chair was acquired at an estate clearance last fall...
extraStory.author: Sarah Sterling
extraStory.content:
The owner of the rental property from which Sir Sits-a-Lot escaped issued a formal apology to the city council today.

'Our only intention was providing a cozy reading nook. We had no idea the chair harbored extreme military ambitions,' they added.
